scope: byte mode, error correction level M, versions 1-10 (up to 154 codewords). Zero dependencies.
verified: GF(256) against its defining properties: exp/log inverse across the field, a^255 = 1, multiplication commutative and associative, every non-zero element has an inverse

Reed-Solomon by SYNDROME EVALUATION — mathematically independent of the polynomial division used to encode, so it is a real check and not a round-trip through the same bug. A deliberately corrupted codeword is asserted to FAIL the check, so the check can demonstrably fail.
format information against BCH(15,5) minimum distance: all 32 valid strings differ in >= 7 bits

structure: module counts per version, three finder patterns correctly formed, NO fourth finder (orientation), alternating timing patterns, dark module, no placeholder surviving into output, mask actually varies with content
NOT_verified: that a phone camera reads it. There is no scanner in this environment. This is a real-device check and it is OPEN.
mitigation: Because the optics are unverified, renderSVG() is never the only path: the pairing UI always shows the code as text and always offers manual entry. If the QR is wrong, nobody is stranded.
failure_modes: content over version 10 at level M -> throws, naming the limit. Never silently truncated.
unsupported version requested -> throws, naming the supported range
status: implemented — 23/23 in test/qr.test.mjs. The maths is checked hard; the optics are not checked at all, and that is stated rather than implied.
